_about: US decision trees, one per catalogue change. A node either asks a question (ask + on) or gives an outcome (cat + src + at + why). bioSrc/bioAt replace the citation when the product is a biologic. note marks a simplification the learner sees.

yes.why: A filling line already approved for aseptic manufacture of other products, with no change to the validated process, is a CBE-30 for a biologic.

no.why: A new or changed facility or filling line that may affect sterility assurance needs prior approval for a biologic.
Adding or replacing a manufacturing facility for a biologic needs prior approval.
no.note: Simplified: the guidance has a few lower-category facility cases; the app treats non-sterile biologic facility moves as prior approval.

yes.why: The new site has never been inspected by FDA for this type of operation (or restarts it after more than two years), so the move needs prior approval.

no.why: The new site does not have a satisfactory CGMP inspection for this type of operation.

yes.why: Aseptic manufacture moves to a new or refurbished area, or to one that does not make similar approved products.

no.why: A move to an existing aseptic area that already makes similar approved products is a moderate change.

yes.why: A terminally sterilized product moving to a new or existing building on the same site is a minor change.
A terminally sterilized product moving to a newly constructed facility at a different site needs prior approval.

no.why: A move to an existing, satisfactorily inspected facility at another site is a moderate change.

yes.why: The product's formulation modifies the rate of availability (modified release), so a move of its manufacture needs prior approval.
The primary packaging controls the dose delivered, so a move needs prior approval.

no.why: A move to a satisfactorily inspected site, not otherwise provided for in the guidance, is a moderate change.

yes.why: Adding or replacing a drug substance manufacturing facility for a biologic needs prior approval.
The new site has never been inspected for this type of operation, or restarts it after more than two years.

no.why: The new site lacks a satisfactory CGMP inspection for this operation.

yes.why: A move of drug substance manufacture to a satisfactorily inspected site is a moderate change.
A move of the final intermediate's manufacture is a CBE supplement.

no.why: A move for intermediates other than the final intermediate is a minor change.

yes.why: The new site has never been inspected for this type of operation.

no.why: The new site lacks a satisfactory CGMP inspection for packaging.

yes.why: The primary packaging controls the dose delivered.

no.why: A primary packaging move not listed as major (including modified-release solid oral products) is a CBE-30.

tree.why: A move of secondary packaging is a minor change.
A move of labeling operations is a minor change.

yes.why: The new lab uses the approved procedures, commitments are met and it can do the testing, so the move is a CBE-30.

no.why: The conditions for the CBE-30 route are not all met.
no.note: Simplified: the guidance lists the move as CBE-30 only when all three conditions hold. The app treats other cases as prior approval; in practice, meet the conditions first or classify a method change on its own.

tree.why: A move of ink imprinting for solid oral products is a minor change.

yes.why: A new contract sterilizer for packaging components, with a process not materially different, is a minor change.
A different sterilization process that may affect sterility assurance needs prior approval.

no.why: Changes to sterilization of components that alter validated parameters are CBE-30 changes.

yes.why: An alternate filling line already approved for aseptic manufacture, with no change to the validated process, is a CBE-30.

no.why: Adding or modifying a filling line that affects sterility assurance needs prior approval.

yes.why: The line is in a new or refurbished aseptic area, or one that does not make similar approved products.
Changes to aseptic processing equipment that may affect sterility assurance need prior approval.

no.why: An equipment change not otherwise provided for is a CBE-30.

yes.why: The change may affect sterility assurance.

no.why: An equipment change not otherwise provided for is a CBE-30.

yes.why: Even like-for-like equipment needs prior approval when the change may affect sterility assurance.
Replacing equipment with equipment of the same design, operating principle and capacity is an annual report change.

no.why: Equipment of the same design and operating principle is a minor change.

yes.why: Replacing equipment with equipment of the same design, operating principle and capacity is an annual report change.

no.why: Equipment of the same design and operating principle is a minor change.

yes.why: A minor change within validated ranges, on the same equipment, is an annual report change.

no.why: Process changes for a biologic that go beyond minor adjustments need prior approval.

yes.why: A fundamental change in manufacturing technology needs prior approval.
The change may affect the controlled release.

no.why: A process, parameter or equipment change not otherwise provided for is a CBE-30.

yes.why: The change may affect sterility assurance.

no.why: A process, parameter or equipment change not otherwise provided for is a CBE-30.
A process, parameter or equipment change not otherwise provided for is a CBE-30.

yes.why: A minor batch size change on the same equipment, with no parameter change, is an annual report change.

no.why: A batch size increase using different equipment or changed parameters needs prior approval.

yes.why: The scale change may affect sterility assurance.

no.why: A change in scale not otherwise provided for is a minor change.

yes.why: Bulk solution storage time rises by more than 50% beyond validated limits.

no.why: Bulk solution storage time rises by no more than 50%.

yes.why: The scale change may affect the controlled release.

no.why: A change in scale not otherwise provided for is a minor change.
A change in scale not otherwise provided for is a minor change.
no.note: The 2004 guidance supersedes SUPAC-IR's reporting categories for scale; keep the dissolution and stability data SUPAC describes as support.

tree.why: A change in the synthetic route is a fundamental change in manufacturing technology.

yes.why: Changes after the final intermediate, or that may change the impurity profile, need prior approval.

no.why: Other drug substance process or parameter changes are CBE-30.

yes.why: The CBE-30 route excludes the final intermediate; redefining it as a starting material needs prior approval.
yes.note: Simplified: the guidance only states the exclusion; the app treats it as prior approval.

no.why: Redefining an intermediate (not the final one) as a starting material is a CBE-30.

tree.why: A new reprocessing procedure for batches that fail specification needs prior approval.

yes.why: The ink is already used in CDER-approved products.

no.why: The ink is not used in any CDER-approved product.

yes.why: For modified-release products, a pressed code can affect release.

no.why: Adding or deleting a pressed code on a solid product that is not modified release is minor.

tree.why: The order of addition for solutions is a minor change.

yes.why: Filter material or pore size changes may affect sterility assurance.

no.why: Changes to filtration parameters (flow, pressure, time, volume) are CBE-30.

tree.why: A change in sterilization method may affect sterility assurance.
Changes to depyrogenation of components are CBE-30.
Eliminating an in-process filtration that is not the sterilizing filtration is a CBE supplement.
Methods or controls that give more assurance are a CBE supplement.

yes.why: A formulation change for a biologic needs prior approval.

1.why: SUPAC-IR Level 1 composition changes are reported in the annual report.

2.why: SUPAC-IR Level 2 composition changes need prior approval, with comparative dissolution data.

3.why: SUPAC-IR Level 3 changes need prior approval and an in vivo bioequivalence study unless waived.

tree.why: Deleting or reducing a colour or flavour is a SUPAC-IR Level 1 change.
A new strength changes the formulation, which needs prior approval.
tree.note: Simplified: the 2004 guidance does not list new strengths; the app follows its composition rule.

yes.why: Tightening criteria for a biologic because the process or assay improved is a CBE-30.

no.why: Tightening of acceptance criteria is a minor change.

yes.why: Broadening or shifting acceptance criteria for a biologic needs prior approval.
Relaxing a criterion for virus or adventitious agent testing needs prior approval.
Relaxing a criterion to comply with an official compendium is a CBE-30.
Relaxing a criterion for raw materials used before the final intermediate is a CBE-30.
Relaxing an environmental or component microbiological monitoring criterion is a CBE-30.

no.why: Relaxing an acceptance criterion needs prior approval.

yes.why: Deleting a test for a biologic needs prior approval.
Deleting a virus or adventitious agent test needs prior approval.
Deleting a test to comply with an official compendium is a CBE-30.
Deleting a test for raw materials used before the final intermediate is a CBE-30.

no.why: Deleting any part of a specification needs prior approval.

yes.why: Adding or replacing a test in a biologic's specification is listed as a prior approval change.
yes.note: Check the guidance table for your product class; some additions to biologics specifications fall into a lower category.

no.why: Adding a test that gives more assurance is a CBE supplement.

tree.why: A change to comply with an official compendium (other than relaxing or deleting) is minor.

yes.why: Replacing or modifying a procedure in technique, acceptance criteria or performance needs prior approval.

no.why: Minor modifications to a procedure are annual report changes.

yes.why: Editorial changes are excluded from the CBE-30 route and go in the annual report.
yes.note: Simplified: the guidance excludes editorial changes from VIII.C.1.a without naming a category.

no.why: The changed procedure does not give the same or greater assurance.

yes.why: Other changes to a regulatory analytical procedure are CBE-30.

tree.why: Establishing a new regulatory analytical procedure needs prior approval.

yes.why: An alternative procedure with the same or greater assurance is a minor change.

no.why: An alternative procedure that gives less assurance cannot be added as minor.
no.note: Simplified: treated like a new regulatory procedure.

yes.why: A method change for components, packaging, the final intermediate or in-process materials with the same or greater assurance is a CBE supplement.

no.why: The method gives less assurance than the approved one.

yes.why: A raw material method with the same or greater assurance is a minor change.
A weaker method for virus or adventitious agent testing needs prior approval.

no.why: Other raw material method changes are CBE-30.

yes.why: A change in product-contact material needs prior approval.

no.why: A supplier change with no change in materials or dimensions is a CBE-30.

yes.why: The polymer has never been used in an approved product of the same dosage form and route.

no.why: A container closure change not otherwise provided for, that does not affect quality, is a CBE-30.

yes.why: Changes to product-contact materials or dimensions need prior approval.

no.why: A supplier change with no change in materials or dimensions is a CBE-30.

yes.why: Size or shape changes to a sterile drug substance container are CBE-30.

no.why: Container changes for a sterile drug product may affect sterility assurance.

tree.why: Primary packaging that controls the dose delivered needs prior approval to change.

yes.why: For solid oral products, closure changes that give the same or better protection are minor.

no.why: A closure that gives less protection needs prior approval.

yes.why: For non-sterile liquids, closure changes that give the same or better protection are minor.

no.why: A closure that gives less protection needs prior approval.

yes.why: Size or shape changes to a sterile drug substance container are CBE-30.

no.why: Size or shape changes to a sterile drug product container may affect sterility assurance.

yes.why: Size or shape changes to a container for a non-sterile solid are minor.

no.why: Size or shape changes for a non-sterile, non-solid product, with no closure change, are a CBE supplement.

yes.why: A container closure change not otherwise provided for is a CBE-30.
yes.note: Simplified: the guidance lists count changes only for non-sterile products.

yes.why: Changing the number of units in a unit-of-use container is a CBE-30.
Changing the count of a non-sterile solid in a multiple-unit container is minor.

no.why: Changing the labeled amount of a non-sterile, non-solid product in a multiple-unit container is a CBE supplement.

tree.why: Changing, adding or deleting a desiccant is a CBE supplement.

yes.why: Blister materials already used in approved products of the same type make this minor.

no.why: Other container closure changes that do not affect quality are CBE-30.
no.note: If the new blister gives less protection, it needs prior approval (IX.B.6).

tree.why: Deleting secondary packaging that gives extra protection needs prior approval.
A flip-seal cap colour change consistent with any colour coding is minor.

yes.why: For a biologic, an extension based on full commercial batch data under an approved protocol is a CBE-30.

no.why: An extension without an approved protocol needs prior approval.

yes.why: Full shelf-life data on production batches under the approved protocol make this an annual report change.

no.why: An extension based on a new or revised protocol, or without full data, needs prior approval.

tree.why: Reducing the expiration dating period to give more assurance is a CBE-30.

yes.why: Adding time points, or deleting time points beyond expiry, is minor.

no.why: Other changes to an approved stability protocol need prior approval.

tree.why: Changing the labeled storage conditions needs prior approval.
Replacing an in-house reference standard under the approved protocol is minor.
A new indication needs prior approval, as an efficacy supplement with clinical data.
Expanding or contracting the population based on data needs prior approval.
Changes to clinical pharmacology or clinical study sections based on new data need prior approval.

yes.why: Adding or strengthening safety information on newly acquired information may go in at once, as a CBE supplement.

no.why: Without newly acquired information that meets the standard, a labeling change needs prior approval.

tree.why: Adding or strengthening an instruction on dosage and administration for safer use is a CBE supplement.
Deleting false, misleading or unsupported indications or claims is a CBE supplement.
Respond to FDA's notification within 30 days with a labeling supplement proposing the change, or a statement of why it is not warranted.
tree.note: Simplified: the app files the response as a prior approval labeling supplement; FDA's letter may ask for a different route. Read the notification.

yes.why: An ANDA must keep the same labeling as the reference listed drug; updates to match it are usually filed as a CBE supplement.
yes.note: This follows FDA's usual practice for generic labeling updates; check current Office of Generic Drugs advice for the change in hand.

no.why: Only ANDAs follow a reference listed drug; for an NDA treat this as an ordinary labeling change.

tree.why: Editorial or similar minor labeling changes go in the annual report.
A label layout change with no content change is minor.
A comparability protocol is submitted in a prior approval supplement (or in the original application); once approved it can lower the category of the change it covers.

CBE30.why: The approved protocol set a CBE-30 for this change.

CBE0.why: The approved protocol set a CBE supplement for this change.

AR.why: The approved protocol set an annual report for this change.

tree.why: Changes that need in vivo bioequivalence studies need prior approval.
A new master cell bank or master virus seed needs prior approval.

yes.why: A working cell bank made under an approved protocol falls in a lower category.
yes.note: Simplified: the app uses the annual report; check the guidance table for your product.

no.why: A working cell bank without an approved protocol needs prior approval.

yes.why: Minor changes to purification parameters are annual report changes.

no.why: A new or revised purification step, resin, column size or loading scale needs prior approval.

tree.why: Changing a virus removal or inactivation method needs prior approval.
The former owner and the new owner each send FDA a letter; the new owner commits to the application's conditions.
tree.note: For BLAs the licence is reissued to the new holder; the app keeps one route for both.

tree.why: A name or address change without a change in ownership is notified by letter; labeling that shows the name is then updated.
tree.note: Simplified: the label update itself may be an annual report item.

yes.why: An alternative source using the same synthesis, at a site with satisfactory CGMP status, is handled like a move of drug substance manufacture to another site: a CBE-30.
yes.note: FDA reviews the drug master file with the supplement. Where the DMF has not been reviewed before, many holders file a prior approval supplement.

no.why: The new source does not have a satisfactory CGMP inspection for this operation.
A source with a different synthesis or new impurities is a change in the synthesis of the drug substance that may affect its impurity profile or properties: prior approval.

yes.why: The new lab uses the approved procedures, commitments are met and it can do the testing, so the move is a CBE-30.
yes.note: The US has no separate batch release site (there is no qualified person). FDA treats a laboratory doing release testing as a testing site.

no.why: The conditions for the CBE-30 route are not all met.
no.note: The US has no separate batch release site (there is no qualified person). FDA treats a laboratory doing release testing as a testing site.

tree.why: Removing a site from the application, with an approved site doing the same work, has minimal potential to affect quality and is reported in the annual report.
tree.note: Not named in the 2004 guidance; this follows FDA practice for minor site changes.

yes.why: A change in scale with equipment of the same design and operating principle, and no other process change, is a minor change.

no.why: A scale change that also changes the drug substance process is a moderate change.
no.note: Simplified: if the change may affect the impurity profile or physical properties, it is major (VII.B.4).

yes.why: For a biologic, tightening a limit because the process improved is a CBE-30.
yes.note: The app applies the specification entry to in-process limits by analogy.

no.why: Tightening an acceptance criterion, including an in-process one, is a minor change.

yes.why: Widening limits or deleting a test for a biologic needs prior approval.
yes.note: The app applies the specification entry to in-process controls by analogy.

no.why: Relaxing an acceptance criterion or deleting any part of a specification (in-process controls included) is a major change.

yes.why: For a biologic, a longer hold time supported by validated data is a CBE-30.
yes.note: Simplified: the app reads the hold-time cases in the 2021 guidance as moderate when data cover the full time.

no.why: A longer hold time without data covering it may affect product quality: prior approval.

yes.why: Bulk solution storage time rises by more than 50% beyond validated limits.

no.why: Bulk solution storage time rises by no more than 50%.
A longer hold time for a non-sterile intermediate, supported by data, has minimal potential to affect quality.
no.note: Not named in the 2004 guidance for non-sterile products; supported under CGMP and reported in the annual report.

tree.why: Working within the approved design space is not considered a change, so nothing is reported.
A design space is proposed by the applicant and approved by FDA. A new or expanded design space for an approved product is submitted in a prior approval supplement.
Real-time release testing deletes end-product tests and establishes new regulatory procedures (models, PAT): prior approval.
Converting a batch process to continuous manufacturing changes the process, equipment and control strategy: prior approval.
tree.note: FDA encourages early meetings before converting; a comparability protocol can lower the category of later changes.

tree.why: Applications do not usually name excipient suppliers. A new supplier of the same grade that meets the approved specification is qualified under CGMP, with no report.
tree.note: If the application names the supplier, or the excipient controls release or is novel, classify it as a composition or process change.

yes.why: For a modified-release product the coating may control release, so a coating weight change is major.

1.why: SUPAC-IR Level 1 composition changes are reported in the annual report.

2.why: SUPAC-IR Level 2 composition changes need prior approval, with comparative dissolution data.

3.why: SUPAC-IR Level 3 changes need prior approval and an in vivo bioequivalence study unless waived.

tree.why: Adding or removing a score line changes how the product can be used and is described in labeling: prior approval.
tree.note: Simplified: the app treats both directions as prior approval. Generic scoring must match the reference listed drug.

yes.why: A shape change for a modified-release product may affect release.

no.why: A change in tablet shape or size with the same composition and mass is treated as a moderate change; dissolution and labeling (the description) change.
no.note: Simplified: FDA practice varies; the app uses CBE-30 because the product description in labeling changes.

tree.why: Moving an inactive ingredient from an animal source to a vegetable or synthetic source with the same specification has minimal potential to affect quality.
tree.note: Simplified: the app reads this from the 2014 annual report guidance examples for component sources.

yes.why: For a licensed biologic, a new dosage form is a prior approval supplement.

no.why: A new dosage form is a new drug product: it needs a new application (an NDA, or an ANDA for a generic), not a supplement.

tree.why: Adding a test and acceptance criterion that gives greater assurance is a CBE supplement.
tree.note: FDA guidance on control of nitrosamine impurities (Revision 2, 2024) asks for nitrosamine changes to be reported in the appropriate supplement; check it for limits.

tighten.why: Tightening an acceptance criterion is a minor change.

add.why: Adding a test that gives greater assurance is a CBE supplement.

delete.why: Deleting any part of a specification is a major change.

relax.why: Relaxing an acceptance criterion is a major change.

tree.why: Testing only some batches removes the test from routine release, which FDA treats like deleting part of a specification: prior approval.
tree.note: Simplified. A comparability protocol can set a lower category.

yes.why: Minor modifications to a procedure are annual report changes.

no.why: An adjustment within the limits the method allows (for example the system suitability ranges of USP <621>) gives the same assurance and is reported in the annual report.
no.note: Simplified: changes outside allowed adjustments are CBE-30 (VIII.C.1.a).

yes.why: FDA expects prior approval for an alternative sterility test, unless an approved comparability protocol covers it.

no.why: Replacing a microbiological procedure with a validated method that gives the same or greater assurance is a CBE-30.
The new procedure does not give the same or greater assurance.

yes.why: For a sterile product a new component supplier may affect sterility assurance and container integrity: a moderate change.

no.why: A new supplier of the same container closure component, same material and specification, is reported in the annual report.

yes.why: A change to packaging or a device that controls the dose delivered is a major change.

no.why: A change to a co-packaged measuring device that does not control the dose is treated as a moderate change.
no.note: Simplified: device constituents can also bring combination product requirements.

tree.why: A change to a component that does not touch the product and has no protective role has minimal potential to affect quality.

yes.why: For a biologic, an extension based on full commercial batch data under an approved protocol is a CBE-30.
yes.note: The app applies the drug product expiration dating entries to the drug substance re-test period by analogy.

no.why: An extension without an approved protocol needs prior approval.
no.note: The app applies the drug product expiration dating entries to the drug substance re-test period by analogy.

yes.why: Full shelf-life data on production batches under the approved protocol make this an annual report change.
yes.note: The app applies the drug product expiration dating entries to the drug substance re-test period by analogy.

no.why: An extension based on a new or revised protocol, or without full data, needs prior approval.
no.note: The app applies the drug product expiration dating entries to the drug substance re-test period by analogy.

reduce.why: A shorter in-use period strengthens an instruction for safe use: a CBE supplement.

extendReal.why: A longer in-use period changes the labeled storage conditions: prior approval.

extendModel.why: A longer in-use period changes the labeled storage conditions: prior approval.

yes.why: More restrictive storage is treated like a reduction in dating: a moderate change.
yes.note: By analogy: the guidance has no drug substance storage entry.

no.why: Less restrictive storage conditions need data and assessment: prior approval.
no.note: By analogy with the drug product entry.

tree.why: A new route of administration is an efficacy supplement that needs prior approval.
tree.note: If the new route needs a new dosage form, a new application may be needed instead.

tree.why: A new proprietary name is reviewed by FDA before use: prior approval.
tree.note: FDA reviews proprietary names for safety and promotional concerns.

agreed.why: A REMS revision (editorial changes, or updates already agreed with FDA) can be implemented when FDA receives it.
agreed.note: The US has REMS, not EU-style risk management plans; most products have no REMS.

minor.why: A minor REMS modification is submitted as a CBE-30.
minor.note: The US has REMS, not EU-style risk management plans; most products have no REMS.

new.why: A major REMS modification needs prior approval.
new.note: The US has REMS, not EU-style risk management plans; most products have no REMS.

tree.why: Adding or strengthening safety wording is a CBE supplement.
tree.note: The US has no PSUSA procedure. Wording that FDA itself requests follows section 505(o)(4) (see that entry).

tree.why: Deleting an indication that is not supported, or no longer pursued, from labeling is a CBE supplement.
tree.note: Simplified: deletions for other reasons may need prior approval; talk to the review division.

tree.why: For an approved product, established conditions and their reporting categories are proposed in a prior approval supplement.

yes.why: Changing established conditions or lowering a reporting category needs prior approval.

no.why: An administrative update of the PLCM (for example recording a completed commitment) goes with the next annual report.

prior.why: The PLCM sets prior approval for this established condition.

moderate.why: The PLCM sets a moderate notification (CBE-30) for this established condition.

low.why: The PLCM sets a low notification (annual report) for this established condition.

no.why: Changes to elements that are not established conditions are managed in the quality system and need no report.

delete.why: Withdrawing an approved comparability protocol is reported in the annual report.

minor.why: A minor modification of an approved protocol, not changing its strategy, is treated as a moderate change.

major.why: A major modification of an approved protocol needs prior approval.

yes.why: Adding identical bioreactors or duplicating a train, with no process change, is a CBE-30.

no.why: Scaling up with different equipment or changed parameters needs prior approval.

yes.why: Introducing a material of human or animal origin raises adventitious agent risk: prior approval.
A raw material change that may affect product quality needs prior approval.

no.why: A raw material change with low potential to affect quality is a CBE-30.

lifetime.why: More resin cycles under an approved lifetime protocol is an annual report change.

supplier.why: A different resin or supplier changes the purification step: prior approval.

yes.why: A potency assay on a new principle needs prior approval.
Changing the technique, acceptance criteria or performance of the potency assay needs prior approval.

no.why: Minor modifications to the assay are annual report changes.

tree.why: A formulation change for a biologic needs prior approval.

first.why: New viral clearance claims for steps not tested before need prior approval.

higher.why: Replacement studies showing a higher risk need prior approval.

same.why: Replacement studies with the same or lower risk are treated as a moderate change.

tree.why: A change in the name or address of a site, with no move and no change to operations, is reported in the annual report.
tree.note: FDA also needs the establishment registration updated.

tree.why: A foreign applicant tells FDA of a new US agent by letter.
tree.note: Pharmacovigilance contacts are not reported as a change to the application.

tree.why: Updating labeling for a new established name is filed as a CBE supplement.
tree.note: Simplified: such changes usually follow FDA or USP direction.

strength.why: To stop marketing a strength for good, ask FDA by letter to withdraw approval of it.
strength.note: A temporary stop is reported under section 506C or in the annual report instead.

pack.why: Deleting a container size, with the remaining sizes covering the dosing, is a minor change.
